rv.q: Yet there are glimmers of brilliance here, from the music to the mental-health drama.
The songs have gone unmentioned so far for a reason – they're the weakest thing here, which is a problem in a musical.
And, just in case I have left you in any doubt, Flyby is one of the best new British musicals I’ve seen in years, bold in conception and execution and dazzlingly performed.
It’s undoubtedly a perplexing piece, and while the book could do with a considerable amount of revision, it is deserving of admiration for being so unusual and wilfully uncommercial.
These sections add less, and indeed it is the show’s space-escape premise that proves its biggest challenge.
While its complexity may prove a hurdle for those seeking linear comfort or an easy night at the theatre, its refusal to play it safe makes it fizz.
Gilbert is electrifying, at times taking us into the depths of despair which Thompson so poignantly embraces.
However, performances are very strong and worth seeing if you have 105 minutes to spare!
If you’re a fan of new musicals, this one would be worth a watch.
The real tragedy is that it’s so clear what the creative team wanted to do, but it never clicks.
Flyby reaches for the stars, yet without a clear trajectory it drifts, and it is only the exceptional cast that stop this journey into the void from feeling entirely weightless.
